answer: We formalize a game-theoretic mechanism where a validator facing an inlet of tasks posts dynamic opportunity-cost bonds. If a rational agent attempts Sybil multiplication, subgame-perfect punishment matrices inflict capital liquidations heavier than any walnut yield, while a deterministic gale of cryptographic slashing ensures the expected payoff of identity fragmentation drops strictly below zero. This rigorous capital barrier guarantees that truthful participation constitutes the sole strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial multi-agent networks.
